text:
maya: Heads-up 1 telemetry saw a clear increase in notify_ingest_bytes after the payload change last week. I'm proposing a compact payload (short keys, drop some redundant meta) to reduce bytes/cost. Want to discuss rollout and console UX.

alex: Can you paste a before/after example? Also, Dedicated customers will need compatibility guarantees.

maya: pasted below. Compact flattens 'signal' and shortens keys.

maya: ```
// current payload
{
  "slo_id": "svc-abc",
  "threshold": 0.995,
  "signal": { "p90": 0.997, "p99": 0.999 },
  "routes": [{ "team": "infra", "contact": "#oncall" }],
  "meta": { "env": "prod", "client": "acme" }
}

// compact candidate
{"id":"svc-abc","t":0.995,"s":{"90":0.997},"r":[["infra","#oncall"]],"m":"c:acme"}
```

sam: Critical: console grouping relies on slo_id and route fingerprint. If we accept short keys we must normalize early so downstreams never break.

maya: Agreed. Plan: ingest-normalizer accepts both shapes for 120 days, emits canonical_event_v1 for downstreams. That way console/query APIs see unchanged fields.

alex: Telemetry ask: label metrics with payload_version so we can track adoption. Something like notify_payload_version{ver="compact|full"} and split notify_ingest_bytes by tenant and version.

maya: will add notify_payload_version and a per-tenant adoption gauge. Also expose sample_size and bytes_saved_estimate for the console.

ops-bot: [ALERT] notify_ingest_bytes x3 baseline over 1h @2026-03-21T10:12:00Z for route=tf-notify-ingest-prod

taylor: From UX: we should surface a per-tenant rollout badge on the SLO/alerting card showing adoption % and delta in ingest_bytes. Small badge with hover -> details panel is ideal.

sam: Add a hover that enumerates the normalized keys (sloId, threshold, routeFingerprint) so oncall can quickly verify grouping keys preserved.

alex: API versioning debate: path (/v2/notify) vs header (X-Notify-Payload: compact). I prefer header since it's easier for SDK flips and proxies. Path version gives clearer logs but more client churn.

maya: Header-first approach, with a documented /v2 path for clients who prefer explicit separation. Also return a warning header when compact was accepted: X-Notify-Accepted: compact.

taylor: Rollout checklist for console + alerts:
- Console card: tenant badge, adoption %, estimated bytes saved, link to telemetry details
- Telemetry: notify_payload_version metric + notify_ingest_bytes split by tenant/version
- Ingest: normalization pipeline + validation warnings to logs/slow-query trace
- API: support X-Notify-Payload and return X-Notify-Accepted; fall back if missing
- Rollout policy: per-tenant feature-flag, staged ramp (5% -> 25% -> 75% -> 100%) over 3 weeks

sam: Alerting: during ramp we will see transient deltas in derived SLOs. Propose a suppression rule: suppress SLO-exposure-change alerts for 24h per-tenant if the trigger's correlated with payload_version churn. Annotate the timeline with rollout events so postmortems can associate spikes.

maya: That sounds reasonable. We'll emit an event notify.rollout.start and notify.rollout.step so the alerting system can correlate.

alex: SDK changes: make SDK opt-in via config (enable_compact:true). If server responds with 4xx validation error, SDK should auto-fallback to full payload and log a telemetry event. Add header X-Notify-Accept: compact to indicate preference.

taylor: I'll prototype a compact badge mock and a details flyout with adoption chart + sample normalized payloads. Keeping it minimal at first (badge + link to telemetry) reduces rollout friction.

maya: I'll open the API spec PR, the ingest-normalizer design doc, and a metrics proposal (names + labels). Also create the feature-flag ticket for per-tenant gating.

sam: +1. Please include sample canonical_event_v1 shape in the PR so console folks can wire grouping.

alex: I'll draft the suppression rule and a short rollout playbook (who to CC on incidents, thresholds to abort ramp).

maya: Great. Can we do a 30m sync tomorrow to finalize?

taylor: yes. I'll throw calendar invite and attach mock.

maya: Thanks everyone. I'll link PRs here once opened. :thumbsup:
